text:
Predicates:
Likes(x, y) ::: x likes y.
Bark(y) ::: y barks.
Animal(y) ::: y is an animal.
Dog(y) ::: y is a dog.
Jump(y) ::: y jumps.
HasLegs(y) ::: y has legs.
Terricolous(y) ::: y is terricolous.
Premises:
∀x ∀y (Likes(x, y) → ¬Bark(y)) ::: Jane does not like any animals that bark.
∀x (Dog(x) → (Animal(x) ∧ Bark(x))) ::: All dogs are animals that bark.
∀x ∀y (Likes(x, y) → Jump(y)) ::: Jane likes all animals that jump.
∀x (HasLegs(x) → Jump(x)) ::: If an animal has legs, then it jumps.
∀x (Terricolous(x) → HasLegs(x)) ::: If an animal is terricolous, then it has legs.
Animal(kiki) ::: KiKi is an animal.
¬(Jump(kiki) ∨ HasLegs(kiki)) → (Terricolous(kiki) ∨ HasLegs(kiki)) ::: If KiKi neither jumps nor has legs, then KiKi is terricolous or has legs.
Conclusion:
¬Bark(kiki) ∧ ¬Dog(kiki) ::: KiKi does not bark and he is not a dog.
